queer_characters.name: Sin-Dee Rella
queer_characters.notes: Described explicitly as a transgender sex worker and portrayed by a transgender actress; the source notes critics commended the film's trans representation.

queer_characters.name: Alexandra
queer_characters.notes: Explicitly described as a trans sex worker; her act of care toward Sin-Dee at the laundromat serves as the film's emotional resolution, emphasizing friendship and solidarity rather than tragedy.

queer_creators.name: Kitana Kiki Rodriguez
queer_creators.notes: Described as a transgender actress; one of the first openly transgender actresses to have an Academy Awards campaign launched for her.

queer_creators.name: Mya Taylor
queer_creators.notes: Described as a transgender actress; became the first transgender actress to win a Gotham Award.

contributor_notes: Sin-Dee and Alexandra are explicitly trans; both played by trans actresses (Rodriguez and Taylor), supporting an own-voices tag. Razmik, the Armenian cab driver with a 'secret interest in trans sex workers,' and Chester, who slept with both trans women, are not given explicit queer labels in the source, so I left them out — a maintainer may want to review whether either warrants an inferred entry. Trigger warning for transphobia reflects the slurs and urine-throwing assault near the film's end; a maintainer may consider adding sexual-violence given the sex-work context. Subtitle/audio languages not discussed in source.
